newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies rally to close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies rally to close sharply higher.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rallied sharply from early losses on short covering and commercial support to trade just under limit gains by the close, traders said. Hog futures also recovered on short covering and closed mixed.

Pork bellies ended 1.700 to 1.000 cent per lb higher with February up 1.575 at 76.550 cents. Prices had been down as much as the daily limit in May and July with July setting a new low of 75.500 cents before rallying.
Carryover sell stops hit futures early but short covering developed with commercial buying prompted by firming fundamentals, adding to the runup, traders said.
"Bottom line, hog slaughter was heavy last week but it's not coming in heavy this week," said Dennis Smith, livestock broker with LIT.
Hog slaughter rates are again running under year-ago levels which appears to have sparked enough interest in cash bellies to have cleaned up offerings, cash sources said.
USDA Tuesday estimated the week-to-date hog slaughter at 695,000 head, under 714,000 in the same period a week ago and 704,000 in the year-ago period.

Smith and other analysts also cited technical support that developed after a recent sharp price slide that took values to limit losses in February for two consecutive days and down another 1.600 cent Tuesday before prices turned around.
"We reached a 50 percent correction of the old (up) move today on the open covering developed after the early break, Smith added.
R.J. O'Brien notably bought February, pit sources said.
After the close, the CME reported a net out-movement last week from warehouses outside Chicago of 695,000 lbs, at the high end of analysts expectations of unchanged to out 750,000 lbs.
Hog futures also found technical support and rallied on short covering with deferred contracts leading the way. Prices ended 0.500 cent higher to 0.300 lower with October off 0.175 at 54.625 cents.

October showed resistance on current cash weakness, but cash ideas firmed. Cash hog prices are now seen firming later this week as producers are expected to hold back hogs in order to force higher packer bids.
Also, hog runs have not appeared that burdensome, traders said.

Rosenthal Collins, Rand Financials and locals bought October while Refco notably bought December late, sources said. In hog options, R.J. O'Brien sold Feb 70 puts, ADM bought Dec 54/56 straddles and Kasa bought Dec 56/58 call spreads early. Loacls bought Feb calls late, pit sources said.
